subject: Cross-border operational controls Q&A — Novaterra RFP
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@novaterrahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@novaterrahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-25T14:12:00Z
Subject: Novaterra RFP — data export & DPA annex questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP intake. Our legal and privacy teams reviewed the initial DPA annex and flagged a few cross-border topics we need clarified before we proceed to procurement:

- Which transfer mechanisms do you rely on for EU->US processing (SCCs + DPA annex mapping, or reliance on a DPF equivalence)?
- Can you confirm key management options for customer-held keys (BYOK / HSM integrations)?
- We need a short operational control matrix showing where processing happens (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and which safeguards apply (KV cache handling, log retention, model routing).

Would you be able to provide an operational Q&A and any evidentiary artifacts (redacted SOC2, DPA annex PDF, technical controls spreadsheet)? We are aiming to close vendor selection by mid-December.

Appreciate it —
Marta
Marta Lopez
Lead Privacy Counsel, Novaterra Health

From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@novaterrahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, procurement@novaterrahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-26T09:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Novaterra RFP — data export & DPA annex questions

Marta — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a consolidated package to start (Redwood_DPA_Annex_v2.pdf and a technical controls workbook). High-level answers below and we can schedule a short tech+legal call this week if helpful.

- Transfer mechanisms: Redwood supports SCCs (we supply DPA annex mapping) for standard controller-to-processor flows. For customers requiring a DPF-based approach we provide operational evidence and runbook materials we’ve used with other healthcare customers; note DPF acceptance is evaluated case-by-case.

- KMS options: We support customer-managed keys via an HSM-backed KMS integration (BYOK). Keys can be scoped per-customer and are stored in the customer’s KMS tenant; Redwood never has plaintext key material. For Dedicated/Private deployments there’s an option for on-prem HSM.

- Operational controls: the attached spreadsheet (DPF-Operational-Controls.xlsx) maps runtime mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) to controls: where data leaves the region, prefix/KV cache behavior, audit log retention by default, and fallback routing policies.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Annex_v2.pdf; DPF-Operational-Controls.xlsx.

Proposed next steps: 1) quick 30-min call with our privacy/tech lead, 2) we provide redacted SOC2 Type II evidence and a short operational playbook tailored to Novaterra’s residency requirement. 

Are you available Thurs or Fri this week for a 30-min?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-01T11:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Novaterra RFP — data export & DPA annex questions

Jonas — adding a few technical clarifications you can forward to Novaterra so expectations are precise:

1) KMS / BYOK: confirm whether Novaterra wants per-tenant CMK rotation policy or per-app keys. Our current implementation supports both; per-tenant (recommended) gives simplest audit footprint.
2) KV cache persistence: we need to be explicit that prefix cache entries are ephemeral and not written to persistent object stores in hosted mode; in Dedicated/Private we can configure cache persistence policies per-deployment.
3) Model routing & fallback: include note that routing to lower-tier models for graceful degradation retains the same data handling commitments (no third-party data sharing) but may change model weights/quantization (we should call this out in the annex).
4) Logs: default retention is 90 days for telemetry/traces and 365 days for audit logs in Dedicated; hosted defaults to 90 days for both unless customer opts for longer retention as an add-on.

I drafted itemized language for the operational controls spreadsheet — attaching as comments.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@novaterrahealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@novaterrahealth.com, david.chen@novaterrahealth.com
Date: 2026-12-02T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Novaterra RFP — data export & DPA annex questions

Thanks Karthik/Jonas — that is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from legal:

- For SCCs: we need a mapping table that shows which subprocessors and regions are in-scope for each transfer mechanism and an explicit column for whether pseudo-anonymized derived data (embeddings) may be processed outside the EU. Please call out any variance by deployment mode.
- For BYOK: can you confirm if hardware-backed keys (HSM) are available in the Hosted product or only for Dedicated/Private? If hosted, are keys stored in a Redwood-managed tenant or do we provide our KMS account?
- SOC2: please send the redacted report and a contact that can verify evidence during procurement.

We’d like an updated workbook with the mapping table and a short summary we can attach to our internal procurement memo.

Regards,
Marta

From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, procurement@novaterrahealth.com

Subject: Re: Cross-border operational controls Q&A — Novaterra RFP

Marta / team — attached is a consolidated Q&A packet (Novaterra-MA-Notes-20261208.docx) and the redacted SOC2 Type II (SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-redacted.pdf). Highlights and answers inline below, and I’ve pulled the exact mapping table into the spreadsheet under the new tab "Novaterra-Mapping":

- Subprocessors/regions: the mapping table lists current subprocessors, regions of processing, and per-deployment applicability. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS tenancy unless the customer requests BYOK; BYOK (HSM-backed) is available for Hosted after an onboarding validation step. Dedicated and Private support customer-managed HSM keys in their KMS.

- Embeddings/derived data: by default, embeddings derived from customer inputs are treated as customer data and follow the same residency controls; the mapping table shows where derived artifacts may transit for model routing purposes (only to permitted regions listed).

- Evidence & verification: attached redacted SOC2. For procurement validation we can provide a point of contact on our security team: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com. We also included a link to our compliance portal in the doc.

Next steps: 1) please confirm whether Novaterra wants Hosted WITH BYOK enabled (we’ll scope onboarding), 2) if acceptable we’ll prepare the final DPA annex with the Novaterra-specific rows populated, and 3) schedule a 30-min sign-off call with legal + tech.

Thanks — I’ve quoted Karthik’s technical clarifications inline in the doc for traceability.

Best,
Jonas
